statement: Leo has two 10-cent coins and three 2-cent coins. How much money does he have?

choices.misconception: I counted the coins instead of adding up what each coin is worth.
I counted only one of the 10-cent coins, then added the three 2-cent coins.
I counted each 2-cent coin as 1 cent, so the three of them made only 3 cents.
I mixed up the numbers and used three 10-cent coins and two 2-cent coins.

hints: Say what each coin is worth before you add.
Add coins of the same kind first. Count the 10-cent coins in tens, then count the 2-cent coins in twos, then put the two amounts together.
The two 10-cent coins make 20 cents and the three 2-cent coins make 2, 4, 6 cents. Now add 20 and 6.

solutions.reliable: Count the 10-cent coins in tens: 10, 20. Count the 2-cent coins in twos: 2, 4, 6. Together that is 20 + 6 = 26 cents. The idea to keep: money is counted by what each coin is worth, not by how many coins there are.

whyOnTest: Counting money means adding coin values, not coins, and grouping coins of the same kind keeps the adding easy.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
